theory.intro: **Per cent** means **per hundred**. A percentage tells you how many equal parts out of $100$ are included. First identify the whole amount.
facts: $37\%$ means $37$ parts out of every $100$ equal parts.
$100\%$ is the **whole** and $0\%$ is **none**, whatever the size of the whole. A percentage is not a fixed number of objects.
steps: Identify the whole. When it is divided into $100$ equal parts, count or read the number of parts included.
Write that number with a $\%$ sign. If asked for the part not included, subtract the included parts from $100$ first.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Four complete columns give $40$ shaded squares, with $3$ more shaded squares.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}40+3\\&=43\end{aligned}$
$43$ out of $100$ squares are shaded, so $43\%$ is shaded.
(b)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}100-43\\&=57\end{aligned}$
$57$ out of $100$ squares are not shaded, so $57\%$ is not shaded.

workedExamples.question_text:
A class has $29$ students. Every student has completed a task.
Another class has $41$ students. None has completed the task.
What percentage completed the task in each class?
workedExamples.solution_text:
The whole first class completed the task, so $100\%$ completed it.
None of the second class completed the task, so $0\%$ completed it.
The class sizes do not change the percentages for the whole or none.

workedExamples.question_text:
A sports club reports that $62\%$ of its members chose a green jersey.
A student says this must mean $62$ members. Is this always true? Explain what the percentage means.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$62\%$ means $62$ out of every $100$ equal parts of the membership.
It means $62$ members only if the whole club has $100$ members.
The club size is not given, so the percentage alone does not tell us the number of members.

workedExamples.question_text:
In a survey of $100$ students, $36$ chose cycling.
(a) What percentage chose cycling?
(b) In this survey, how many students does $36\%$ represent?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $36$ out of $100$ students chose cycling, so $36\%$ chose cycling.
(b) The whole survey contains $100$ students, so $36\%$ represents $36$ students.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}25+25\\&=50\end{aligned}$
$50$ parts out of $100$ are shaded, so $50\%$ is shaded.

workedExamples.question_text:
A cake is cut into $100$ equal pieces. At a party, $26$ pieces are eaten, then another $35$ pieces are eaten.
What percentage of the cake remains?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Pieces eaten:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}26+35\\&=61\end{aligned}$
Pieces remaining:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}100-61\\&=39\end{aligned}$
$39$ out of $100$ pieces remain, so $39\%$ of the cake remains.

development.question_text:
A $100$-square grid has $72$ squares shaded.
What percentage is **not** shaded?

development.solution_text:
Three sections are shaded. Each contains $25$ parts.
$25+25+25$
$=75$
$75$ parts out of $100$ are shaded, so the shaded percentage is $75\%$.

development.question_text:
In a survey of exactly $100$ households, $15\%$ had no pets.
How many households had at least one pet?
development.solution_text:
$100-15$
$=85$
$85$ households had at least one pet.

mastery.question_text:
A target is to complete $104$ visits. All $104$ visits are completed.
What percentage of the target is completed? Explain.
mastery.solution_text:
All the target visits are completed, so the whole target is completed.
The percentage completed is $100\%$, even though the whole contains $104$ visits.

mastery.question_text:
A cake is cut into $100$ equal pieces. At a party, $48$ pieces are eaten, then another $39$ pieces are eaten.
What percentage of the cake remains?
mastery.solution_text:
$48+39$
$=87$
$100-87$
$=13$
$13$ out of $100$ pieces remain, so $13\%$ of the cake remains.
